## Solution

**Setup.** An equilateral triangle of side $n=10$ is divided into $100$ unit equilateral triangles by the triangular grid. The grid lines run in three directions, each pair meeting at $60°$. A rhombus in this grid must have its four sides along grid lines; opposite sides are parallel, so the sides use exactly two of the three directions. By the $3$-fold symmetry of the equilateral triangle, all three orientations contribute equally, so we count rhombuses of one orientation and multiply by $3$.

**One orientation.** Fix two grid directions $\mathbf{e}_1, \mathbf{e}_2$ (unit vectors at $60°$). A parallelogram with sides $a\,\mathbf{e}_1$ and $b\,\mathbf{e}_2$ has side lengths $a$ and $b$; it is a **rhombus** iff $a = b$. Set the common side length to $s \ge 1$.

Place the triangle with lattice coordinates $i \ge 0,\; j \ge 0,\; i+j \le n$. A rhombus of side $s$ has vertices
$$(i,j),\quad (i+s,j),\quad (i,j+s),\quad (i+s,j+s).$$
The binding constraint is the top vertex: $i+s+j+s \le n$, i.e. $i+j \le n-2s$. The number of valid positions $(i,j)$ with $i\ge0, j\ge0, i+j\le n-2s$ is the triangular number
$$\frac{(n-2s+1)(n-2s+2)}{2}, \qquad s = 1, 2, \dots, \left\lfloor n/2\right\rfloor.$$

**Computation for $n=10$.** Summing over $s=1,\dots,5$:

| $s$ | $(n{-}2s{+}1)(n{-}2s{+}2)/2$ | value |
|-----|-------------------------------|-------|
| 1 | $9\cdot10/2$ | 45 |
| 2 | $7\cdot8/2$ | 28 |
| 3 | $5\cdot6/2$ | 15 |
| 4 | $3\cdot4/2$ | 6 |
| 5 | $1\cdot2/2$ | 1 |

$$\text{Per orientation} = 45+28+15+6+1 = 95.$$

**Verification (unit rhombuses).** A unit rhombus ($s=1$) is two adjacent triangles sharing an interior edge. Total edge-incidences: $100\times3=300$; boundary edges: $3\times10=30$; interior edges $= (300-30)/2 = 135$. Formula gives $3\times45=135$. ✓

**Total.** Multiplying by the three orientations:

$$\boxed{3 \times 95 = 285}.$$
